text: The rebalancing run record is read as one GET on the rwb-case contract for a business date, answering the move count of the run and the case IDs of the moves; until RWB-P3-E1030-CON publishes it, the story uses the placeholder of rule 8 and describes the comparison, not the operation.
why: The reconciliation needs a comparable count of moves, and no source names the run record operation or its fields.
read: FSD P3 A2.17; TSD P3 T3.1; RWB-E1-030 sections 4 and 12
confirm: Solution architect, P3, when RWB-P3-E1030-CON is published
impact: If the contract answers per case instead of per run, the move count is taken from the case list of the run; the story is buildable against the fake either way.

text: The ledger count break is a row on the reconciliation break list of rwb-case with the business date, the two counts and the case ID of the missing move, addressed to the data steward RW-DATASTEW; its message ID, text and check name are left as the placeholder of rule 8 until the P7 message set is fixed.
why: A difference has to be visible to the data steward, and no source gives the message or the check name of this break.
read: FSD P7 A2.6 (MSG-P1-019, REC-08); RWB-E1-030 section 14 and AC9
impact: Documentation only: the break listing and its content are fixed here; the message identifier changes when the message set is agreed.

text: The actions payload holds the keys reason, ruleId, ruleVersion, queueId and ownerUserId, and the rule ID and rule version are the ones of the queue's ASSIGNMENT row in force at the run; the concrete rule ID and version values are not invented here.
why: The entry has to explain itself, and neither the payload keys nor an assignment rule row are given in the sources.
read: TSD P7 T3.1 (DF-DEC-014); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 16 and slide 27
confirm: Solution architect, P7, with the decision-record library schema
impact: The payload shape is fixed at build; no business value depends on it, because the values arrive in the record.

text: The count of a business date is read once per final call the rebalance records, with the decision filter set to CASE_TRANSFERRED and then to OWNER_ASSIGNED, and the business date expressed as its first and last instant in from and to; the count of the day is the sum of the two totals.
why: The read has to be fixed to be testable, and no source says which value the decision filter takes or how a business date maps to the range.
read: TSD P7 T-A API-P7-006; TSD P7 T3.2 LOV-DECISION
impact: If the filter keeps decision codes only, one rebalance decision code is added to LOV-DECISION and one call replaces the two; the criterion stays the same.
